media.author: Nico Portuondo and Anthony Cruz
media.title: Senate negotiators reach deal on permitting text
media.summary: First report that the four Senate negotiators had a deal on text. Heinrich and Whitehouse were holding back endorsements while they discussed 'the last five yards,' and Democrats still had doubts about Trump's commitment to more renewable projects. Text was expected that week.

quote.text: We have reached a deal on text
quote.speaker: An aide for Sen. Martin Heinrich, speaking anonymously

media.author: Nico Portuondo
media.title: Senate bipartisan permitting deal faces a House buzz saw
media.summary: House Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman said most House Democrats will not support the Senate bill as written and urged talks to resume after the midterms. The report says Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie had not endorsed it.

quote.text: Folding our hand now or in the lame duck makes no sense when we can keep working on this and, in a few more months, have a much better deal that works for everyone.
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.)

media.author: Amelia Davidson
media.title: Democrats gear up to tank data center legislation
media.summary: Senate Democrats prepared to sink the House-passed Ratepayer Protection Act at a Wednesday cloture vote. Schumer called it a fraud and pointed to the Van Hollen and Heinrich bills as stronger options.

quote.text: We’re very united in opposition to the bill, whether it’s on cloture or at some other point
quote.speaker: Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.)

media.author: Nico Portuondo and Amelia Davidson
media.title: Permitting won't get vote ahead of election
media.summary: Senate negotiators did not close a deal that week, so a permitting vote would wait until after the elections. Democrats wanted more review time and firmer assurances that the administration would stop attacking clean energy projects. The story lists Section 401, NEPA limits and NHPA as likely parts of any package.

quote.text: we need just a bit more clarity on exactly what return to regular order for wind and solar projects looks like
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

media.author: Inside Congress staff
media.title: Capitol agenda: One day more? (Inside Congress live updates)
media.summary: Live-update page for the day the bill text was due and the Ratepayer Protection Act went to a cloture vote. A summary of the permitting package had circulated and senators wanted the text, especially on issues that could decide votes in a lame-duck session. The cloture vote failed 57-43; four Democrats joined all Republicans in favor.

quote.text: All the issues are solved in concept
quote.speaker: Sen. Angus King (I-Maine)

media.author: Josh Siegel
media.title: Trump will green-light wind energy projects to strike permitting deal
media.summary: Trump told advisers he would direct the Defense Department to start clearing its queue of delayed onshore wind projects to close a permitting deal. Thune had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal so a bill could move before senators left to campaign.

quote.text: President Donald Trump signaled he would ease his administration's blockade on renewable energy projects to entice Democrats to agree to a permitting deal.
quote.speaker: POLITICO Pro (Josh Siegel)

media.author: Josh Siegel
media.title: Permitting talks reach 'final' stages
media.summary: Capito said a deal was very close and Whitehouse said talks were in their final wrap-up, with the hardest issues resolved last. Capito conceded the floor vote could slip a week from the timeline she and Thune had set.

quote.text: in final wrap up, but some of the most difficult issues are the last ones resolved
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

media.author: Nico Portuondo, Amelia Davidson and Pavan Acharya
media.title: Senate roadblock sparks new competition over data center bills
media.summary: After Heinrich objected to Husted's unanimous-consent request on the Ratepayer Protection Act, Blumenthal and Hawley pitched their GRID Act in a letter to Energy and Natural Resources leaders. The story frames the House-passed bill as stalled in the Senate.

quote.text: those hopes were dashed Thursday after Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) objected to Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-Ohio) unanimous consent request
quote.speaker: POLITICO

media.author: Josh Siegel
media.title: Debate over preservation law tripping up permitting talks
media.summary: Mike Lee's push to change the National Historic Preservation Act had become a major sticking point. Lee wanted limits on lawsuits; some Democrats were wary because the law matters to tribes and preservation groups. Heinrich said the aim was to preserve the law's intent while making reviews more predictable.

quote.text: how do you find that balance of where you preserve the intent, but make things more predictable and efficient?
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

media.author: Josh Siegel
media.title: Permitting deal deadline remains elusive
media.summary: The August recess goal for a deal was slipping. Democratic negotiators were pressing for transmission measures and limits on the administration's power to cancel approved projects; King said the administration had to take its thumb off the scale.

quote.text: until the administration takes their thumb off the scale, we’re not going to be able to do it
quote.speaker: Sen. Angus King (I-Maine)

media.author: Miranda Willson
media.title: Groups urge lawmakers to protect state water reviews in permitting talks
media.summary: Nearly 60 national and regional groups wrote to the Senate EPW Committee against limiting state and tribal Section 401 water reviews. Republicans and the administration say blue states have used Section 401 to slow or block energy projects.

quote.text: Environmental advocates are pushing back on a top Republican priority in ongoing energy permitting reform negotiations.
quote.speaker: E&E News (Miranda Willson)

media.author: Josh Siegel
media.title: Where the permitting talks stand
media.summary: Advocates warned that senators were running out of time to reach a deal by the August recess. Staff from the ENR and EPW committees met during the July Fourth recess week. ACP's Jason Grumet said the window was starting to close.

quote.text: The window of opportunity there is starting to close this Congress
quote.speaker: Jason Grumet, American Clean Power Association

media.author: Nico Portuondo
media.title: New England gas crunch puts Sheldon Whitehouse in a bind
media.summary: High power prices and offshore wind delays had New England Democrats split on new gas pipelines. Whitehouse, a lead permitting negotiator, said the pipeline question needed consideration.

quote.text: the pipeline question requires some consideration
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

media.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
media.title: The Senate reaches a permitting deal (Heatmap AM, item 1)
media.summary: Heatmap's morning newsletter led with the Senate deal on text. Whitehouse told Politico he needed more clarity from the administration on easing its blockade of wind and solar approvals. Text was due that week.

quote.text: Neither Democrats nor Republicans released text of the bill, which both parties said should come out this week.
quote.speaker: Heatmap AM

media.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
media.title: Permitting Reform Talks Trail Off
media.summary: Reports that talks stalled on Sept. 24 and that the White House signaled its concessions may not outlast November. Betting markets still gave permitting reform about a 78 percent chance of passing before 2027.

quote.text: The White House, meanwhile, has indicated that President Donald Trump’s concessions to Democrats to make the bill may no longer be on the table after November.
quote.speaker: Heatmap AM

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: The Wright Interview and Permitting's Peril
media.summary: Meyer summarizes the week: the White House wanted a quick deal, Senate Democrats slowed down on Sept. 23, and Heinrich and Whitehouse said getting the deal right mattered more than election-year deadlines. He argues Democrats should not let the chance pass.

quote.text: We believe there is a good deal to be had
quote.speaker: Sens. Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse, joint statement

media.author: Jael Holzman
media.title: Offshore Wind's Existential Crisis at Climate Week
media.summary: California and New York officials said at Climate Week that the administration's offshore wind actions were illegal, while NYSERDA's CEO said litigation could not fix investor doubts. It also records Wright declining to confirm Politico's report that Trump would lift the wind blockade.

quote.text: I do believe a successful permitting reform thing changes the playing field for anything you want to build in this country, including wind.
quote.speaker: Energy Secretary Chris Wright

media.author: Matthew Zeitlin
media.title: What's a Utility to Do When Everyone Is Mad at Them?
media.summary: Industry insiders told Heatmap that utilities' political weakness is one reason a deal could pass, because interregional transmission reform could threaten utility spending in their own territories. EEI has backed permitting reform publicly since last year.

quote.text: They are gonna get smoked in the Senate permitting deal
quote.speaker: An energy industry figure following the negotiations, anonymous

media.author: Matthew Zeitlin
media.title: The Bipartisan Buddies With a Plan to Fix Transmission
media.summary: Reps. Gabe Evans and Scott Peters released the CLEAR Act, which would apply to transmission lawsuits the stricter standards used for gas and hydropower projects. Peters expected a Senate package to include NEPA changes, limits on presidents canceling projects, and Section 401 reform.

quote.text: I think it’s coming together pretty well
quote.speaker: Rep. Scott Peters (D-Calif.)

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: Meta Down, Permitting Odds Up
media.summary: Meyer lays out the six buckets of a likely deal (NEPA and judicial review, transmission, Clean Water Act, permit certainty, historic preservation, everything else) and says Lee's NHPA interest comes from his committee's jurisdiction. Prediction markets jumped to 77 percent that day.

quote.text: A permitting reform deal will probably have six buckets.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer, Heatmap

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: What a Permitting Reform Deal Could Look Like (Shift Key, with Daniel Palken)
media.summary: Arnold Ventures' Daniel Palken walks through the history of permitting deals and the six buckets of the current talks, which he calls four-corner negotiations among the EPW and ENR leaders. He says the administration's cancellations and withheld permits are the biggest obstacle to Democratic buy-in.

quote.text: all four parties are really sincerely interested in good faith in getting to a deal
quote.speaker: Daniel Palken, Arnold Ventures

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: Permitting Reform, Data Centers, and More With Senator Heinrich and Secretary Granholm (Shift Key)
media.summary: Recorded in late July. Heinrich said talks were active and that the White House was the biggest wild card, citing new historic preservation regulations, offshore wind stop-work orders and the Pentagon's halt on wind reviews. He also described his connect-and-manage interconnection bill and said he would 'get what you can done' in this Congress.

quote.text: I think the biggest wild card is actually and challenge is the White House because the White House continues to do things that sort of poison the well.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: Scoop: A Key Democrat Wants to Break America's Worst Energy Bottleneck
media.summary: Heinrich introduced a bill letting new power plants of any type skip full interconnection studies in exchange for curtailing output when the grid is congested, copying the Texas approach. Heatmap saw it as the kind of technology-neutral bill that could slot into a permitting package.

quote.text: would make it easier for new power plants to hook up to electricity markets across the country
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

media.author: Robinson Meyer
media.title: Freedom (It Won't Slow You Down)
media.summary: Cortez Masto and Cotton released a Senate version of the FREEDOM Act that keeps future presidents from interfering with permitted projects. It dropped the House bill's $5 million de-risking compensation and lets a court appoint a contractor to finish a stalled permit. Heatmap calls such a provision essential to any deal.

quote.text: Most importantly, it jettisons a de-risking compensation program.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

media.author: Matthew Zeitlin
media.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act
media.summary: Explains why hyperscalers back the bill. Harvard's Ari Peskoe calls the PURPA standard largely symbolic because Congress cannot force state regulators to act, and analysts say data centers are not yet the main driver of past price increases.

quote.text: largely symbolic
quote.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School

media.author: Matthew Zeitlin
media.title: FERC Has a New Plan for Data Centers
media.summary: FERC voted 5-0 to send show cause orders to six grid operators, covering study rules, cost-shift safeguards, co-location, flexible service and proximate generation. FERC chose region-by-region orders over a national rule.

quote.text: If new infrastructure is built to accommodate a data center, and that data center doesn’t show up, residential customers are not left on the hook to pay the costs
quote.speaker: FERC Commissioner David Rosner

media.author: Jael Holzman
media.title: How Has the Rise of AI Changed the Odds of a Permitting Deal? (Q&A with ACORE's Ray Long)
media.summary: ACORE's Ray Long says data center load is a catalyst for permitting reform. He cites 166 gigawatts of needed power over four years, about half for data centers, and says a bill would have to come from a Senate deal in an election year.

quote.text: The data center load is a part of the catalyst to get people talking about it
quote.speaker: Ray Long, ACORE
